newsitem.title: SPAIN: GOLF-KITE AND BALLESTEROS SHARE COMMON AIM.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-KITE AND BALLESTEROS SHARE COMMON AIM.

text.p: Ryder Cup captains Tom Kite and Seve Ballesteros are both keen to play in next September's renewal at Valderrama.

The pair, competing in a pro-am event this week before Kite pays a visit to Valderrama on Monday and Tuesday, share a belief the roles of player and captain can be combined, assuming their form is good enough at the time.
"I will try and get into the team, but there is still a long way to go and, by next August when I must make decisions, I will see how I'm feeling," said Ballesteros.
Kite commented: "It would be a great honour to make the team as both player and captain. I would like to be playing well enough to be in a position to do that.

"Like Seve, I've not had a great season and we both need to play a bit better. It's been a long time since there was a playing captain. Dai Rees captained the Great Britain team in 1961 and Arnold Palmer was the last American playing captain in 1963.
"But there has been no playing captain since Europeans were included in 1979. Whether a player can be both player and captain remains to be seen."
Kite, who is captaining the United States team for the first time, halved with Ballesteros in their singles clash in the 1985 match at the Belfry.
He joked it would nice to play again next year, although the Spaniard insists home advantage will work heavily in Europe's favour.

Kite retorted: "That's what we thought at Oak Hill last year and we lost. Being hometown heroes doesn't always guarantee success. But the Ryder Cup has been 50-50 since 1983. It's the flip of a coin."
Tiger Woods, the latest American phenomenon who last weekend won the Las Vegas Invitational tournament, has yet to earn any Ryder Cup points.
"He can do that when he has signed all the papers making him an exempt US Tour player," said Kite. "But I'm sure he will have done that by the time I get back."
